doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Teaching books and his place as father of jazz flute
summary: His books Jazz Flute Conceptions and Jazz Improvisation, a few students, and his claim as a flute pioneer.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well have you done any private teaching? Do you pass on any of this to students?

I do have two books out you know. I had one I think is out of print, Jazz Flute Conceptions, and the other one I got a lot of good response from some good musicians on Metamorphosis. It used to be Metamorphosis, written about the 1970s, and then Time Warner or Warner Publications, they changed the name to Jazz Improvisation. Unfortunately they left out the — they put a CD with it, like a play along, but they left out the information in the front, the information in the back, they just said, “People know that already” which I wish they hadn’t done that. And I just have a few students here and there. I don’t really have a place that I can teach so I just maybe sometimes teach at a store or that type of thing. I haven’t give up yet, I’m still playing.

I hope to keep making each, each time you play like what do they say, you’re as good as your last solo or something like that? So each time you play you keep trying to play some good music and so I played a gig the other day and my alto sounded good, the tenor sounded good, the alto flute, I’ve been playing alto flute lately because it has a nice warm sound on the flute, and my last gig was I had a lot of nice compliments. So you live compliment to compliment.
Yeah. And you have a nice niche in jazz history I think. And I think that’s nice.

Oh that’s nice, yeah. Yes that’s my claim. I was one of the, they call me the father of jazz flute, or one of the early pioneers of jazz flute, and I’m still trying to hang in there and play some good music. I hope to re-record it again before the millennium. Boy that’s almost another year, maybe the end of the millennium, whatever you call it.
